featured_videos.title: You CAN EAT A LOT and STILL LOSE WEIGHT and CONTROL BLOOD SUGAR! Delicious, Low Calorie & Low Carb
featured_videos.creator: Patricia Delicious Nutrition
featured_videos.editorial_title: Eat More, Lose Weight? Low Carb Makes It Work
featured_videos.commentary: Over 100k views on a veggie casserole recipe tells you something pretty interesting: the low-carb crowd is massive and hungry for practical meal ideas, even when it's not strictly carnivore. Patricia Delicious Nutrition found the sweet spot between approachable and actually useful. The core message, that you can eat a decent volume of food and still manage blood sugar, is something carnivores talk about constantly but this video reaches people who aren't quite in the meat-only camp yet. Worth a watch here if you've got a friend who's low-carb-curious but not ready to go full carnivore.

featured_videos.title: Cheesy Breadsticks That Help Me Thrive on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Emmathecarnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Emma keeps it simple: cheese, egg, seasoning. That's it. What's interesting here isn't just the recipe, it's what the comments reveal about how people actually eat carnivore long-term. People are using this as a pizza crust, a burger bun, a vehicle for more fat. The community has essentially crowdsourced a dozen variations in the comment section alone. If you're hitting a texture rut and missing something bread-like, watch it here and check the comments for ideas people have already tested.

featured_videos.title: Top 5 Foods I Eat on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: Real talk: whenever Shawn Baker posts a "top foods" video, the comments become their own whole thing. People show up with their lists, their hot takes, their "but what about organ meat" arguments, and it's genuinely one of the better comment sections in carnivore YouTube. Beef, bacon, eggs, and salmon are dominating everyone's answers this week, which lines up with pretty much every "what I eat" post on Reddit too. It's weirdly reassuring when the community converges like this. Watch it here and drop your own top 5 in the comments.

featured_videos.title: Cheap HI FAT carnivore staple! My GO-TO MEAL almost every day
featured_videos.creator: Mitch Weiss, OGC, Healthy Aging
featured_videos.editorial_title: Bacon Fat Is the Secret to Eating Carnivore at 63
featured_videos.commentary: Mitch has been doing this for five years and he's 63. That context matters. A lot of the carnivore conversation centers on younger folks, but the metabolic case for high fat eating actually gets stronger as we age. Bacon rendered in its own fat, eggs cooked in the drippings -- it sounds indulgent until you understand that dietary fat is essential for hormone production, brain function, and fat-soluble vitamin absorption. The top comment pointing out that the adult brain is roughly 60% fat isn't trivia, it's the whole argument. Watch it here if you want a grounded, no-frills look at what sustainable carnivore eating can look like decades in.

featured_videos.title: I Tweaked My Carnivore Diet and It's Working!
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: Protocol Tweaks That Actually Move the Needle
featured_videos.commentary: 291 comments on under 10k views. That ratio tells you everything. When someone documents real protocol adjustments and shares results, the community shows up. Carnivore Quest isn't selling a starting point, they're showing iteration in action, which is what year-two carnivores actually need. Stop treating carnivore like a static protocol and start treating it like a system you test. Watch it here and pay attention to what they changed and why.

featured_videos.title: The Carnivore Diet Finally Got Reviewed -- Here's What They Found (New Study)
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: What a New Carnivore Study Actually Found
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Tony Hampton is a metabolic health physician and he's walking through the actual findings of a recent carnivore diet review -- which is exactly the kind of content this community needs more of. Anecdotes are powerful, but peer-reviewed data is what moves the needle on credibility. If you've ever wanted to send a skeptical friend or doctor something grounded, this is a good candidate. Watch it here and pay attention to how he handles the nuance -- he doesn't oversell, which is why it's worth your time.
